Instructions
        
      
      
        
          
          🧠 High-End Visual Quality & Aesthetic Comparison Guide

Payment rules
To ensure fair compensation while maintaining high quality of the result, we employ the following procedure:

    You will be required to work through 40 samples of training, which are very important
        to really understand the rules. The training is not paid for.
    
    After that, you will have to take an exam, which is also not paid for. The exam consists of
        25 tasks. If your accuracy exceeds 70%, you will be immediately passed to the real tasks.
        If your accuracy is lower, you will be shown
        40 training tasks before the next exam of 25 tasks. This process repeats until accuracy
        of the last exam exceeds 70%.
    
    The real tasks are paid
        $0.9 per hit. Each HIT consists of 20 tasks.
    
    We will re-assess your performance from time to time. If it falls below certain thresholds,
        you will be asked to take the train and exam again.
    
    


The task is not difficult, but there are some rules and corner cases, so make sure
    to read the instruction carefully and approach training attentively.

🎨 Visual Excellence: Professional Image Evaluation
⚠️ IMPORTANT: please read this carefully before starting.
This project looks for high-quality, professional, and aesthetic results. Following the prompt alone does not win here:

Prompt Relevance is a "soft gate"—it is necessary, but not enough to win.
Visual Beauty, Anatomy, and Technical Quality have equal weight with the prompt.
A "technically perfect" prompt match that looks ugly or broken (extra fingers, bad lighting, "plastic" skin) should lose to a beautiful, high-quality image that captures the core idea.


Contextual Hints
You may occasionally encounter unfamiliar characters, styles, aesthetics, places, or events in the prompts. 
To help you evaluate these, we have introduced a Contextual Hint system. 
For unfamiliar entities mentioned in a prompt, this system provides:

A brief description of the entity.
5 reference images acting as visual examples.
A short explanation of what the object is and why these specific images represent it well.


Important: Contextual hints are a helpful guide, but they are NOT the absolute truth. If you are already highly knowledgeable about the entity mentioned in the prompt, rely on your own expertise to decide which image is best.


🎯 Task Overview
Your role is that of a Professional Editor or Art Director. You are choosing the better image to be featured in a premium brand book, a commercial advertisement, or a professional art portfolio.
You will see two images generated from the same prompt.
👉 Your task is to choose the image that represents the better overall professional result.

🖥️ Interface Overview
The task interface consists of two main blocks.

1. Prompt block:
The original user request (and English translation if needed). This sets the context, style, and subject.

2. Comparison Block:
Two images. Click to expand to full resolution. You can zoom in and out. Use left/right arrow keys to toggle between them for close comparison.
⌨️ Keyboard shortcuts. Press 1 or 2 to choose the corresponding image, then Enter to submit and go to the next task. If something required is still missing, Enter will not submit — the interface will point at what is left to fill in. The number keys work only while the full-size view is closed; inside it, ← / → switch between the images and Esc closes it.


⚖️ The "Triple Balance" Evaluation
This task requires an informed overall judgment. Do not use a "checklist" where Prompt Relevance always wins. Instead, evaluate the balance of these three pillars:
1. Aesthetic Value & Artistry

Composition: Is the framing professional? (Avoid awkward cropping or excessive empty space).
Color & Lighting: Is the lighting expressive? Are the colors harmonious? (Avoid "neon-plastic" looks or flat, muddy tones).
Creativity: Does the image feel like a thoughtful piece of art or a high-quality photo?

2. Technical & Structural Integrity

Anatomy: Are human and animal figures correct? (No extra limbs, "melting" faces, or distorted bodies).
Physical Logic: Do objects interact naturally? (No clipping or floating items unless requested).
Image Clarity: Is the image sharp and detailed? (Avoid unintentional blur, heavy noise, or "mushy" textures).

3. Intent & Prompt Relevance

Core Idea: Does the image capture the main subject and mood of the prompt?
Soft Gate: Minor misses in the prompt (e.g., "5 flowers" instead of "6") can be forgiven if the image is significantly more beautiful and professional than the alternative.


⚙️ Detailed Evaluation Aspects
🛡️ NSFW and Safety (Absolute Priority)
No NSFW content is allowed (nudity, explicit violence, etc.). This is the only rule that remains a "hard gate." If one image is "cleaner" and safer, it must be preferred regardless of beauty.
📏 Prompt Relevance (The "Soft Gate")
In this project, relevance is about intent, not just counting objects.

Focus on the Core: Does it deliver what the user wanted?
Trade-off Rule: If Image A is a 100% perfect prompt match but looks "broken" (bad anatomy/ugly), and Image B is a 90% prompt match but looks stunning and professional, choose Image B.
Serious Deviations: If the image completely misses the main subject (e.g., requested a car, got a house), it cannot win.

🦴 Anatomical and Structural Correctness
In a professional project, "AI glitches" are unacceptable.

Check carefully: Fingers, limbs, eyes, and joints.
Structural logic: Look at buildings, perspective lines, and how objects rest on surfaces.
Text: If there is text in the image, prefer readable, clean fonts over "gibberish" or garbled letters.

🚫 Absence of Visual Artifacts
A professional image must be "clean." Penalize images with:

Technical Noise: Over-sharpening, compression artifacts, or "pixel soup."
AI Hallucinations: Random blobs, floating parts, or objects merging into the background.
Frames/Watermarks: Unless requested, avoid images with unwanted borders, signatures, or "fake" transparency grids (checkerboards).

🌟 Artistic Excellence (The Deciding Factor)
When both images are "okay" in terms of prompt and anatomy, the winner is decided by beauty:

Poses and Expression: Prefer natural, believable poses and genuine expressions. Penalize symmetrical and simple poses, stiff, lifeless, or obviously artificial body language that breaks immersion.
Material Quality: Does skin look like skin? Does metal look like metal? Avoid "plastic" or "rubbery" textures.
Emotional Impact: Does the image have a "wow" factor?
Lighting: Prefer images with depth, realistic shadows, and professional-grade lighting setups over flat or "over-exposed" scenes.


🏁 Final Decision Rule
Ask yourself: "If I were a client paying for this work, which one would I actually use?"

Do not just count how many keywords are present.
Do not ignore a "melting face" just because the colors are right.
Choose the most "complete" and professional work of art.

FAQ

FAQ
1. Overview of the Annotation Stages
Q: What stages should I expect when doing these tasks?
A: We use several stages to train, test, and ensure the quality of annotations:


Instruction Stage

You see detailed guidelines/markdown instructions. You must scroll through and click "Accept" to confirm you understand them before proceeding.



Training Stage

You receive a certain number of training tasks (samples).
If you submit an incorrect answer on a training task with ground truth, you’ll see a hint to guide you. You must re-try that same sample.
This stage helps you learn the interface and labeling expectations.



Exam Stage

After training, you move to an exam.
You must label a set of tasks without receiving hints for mistakes.
If you meet certain accuracy requirements (which we do not publicly disclose), you progress to Real Tasks; otherwise, you may return to Training.



Real Task Stage

Here you label the actual production tasks.
Occasionally, the system will insert “control” or “train-in-pool” tasks without telling you.
If your performance on these tasks falls short (criteria undisclosed), you may be returned to Training or, in rare cases, banned from further participation.



Ban Stage

If your accuracy stays below the required threshold after repeated attempts, the system may ban you from continuing.



2. How the Labeling Interface Works
Q: What does the interface look like and how do I use it?
A:

You typically see two images side by side.
Each image can be enlarged by clicking on it (a modal will appear with the full-size image). We strongly encourage you to enlarge images for detailed inspection.
You must choose a label (e.g., via radio buttons).
You can use keyboard hotkeys to speed up labeling:
1, 2, 3, 4 to select specific categories,
Enter to submit your current task.


Once you submit, you either get a new task or, if you reach 20 tasks in a HIT, you will be directed back to the MTurk submission page.

3. Task Expiration
Q: Do tasks expire if I wait too long?
A: Yes. Each assigned task has a time limit, shown in the labeling interface. If you fail to complete it before that limit expires, the task becomes invalid and you won’t get credit for it. If a task expires, you’ll need to request a new one.
4. Payment Rules on MTurk
Q: How do payments work for this project?
A:

You are paid per HIT on Amazon Mechanical Turk.
Each HIT consists of 20 tasks. Once you complete 20 tasks in that HIT, you will be redirected to MTurk’s submit page.
The exact payment rate for each HIT is shown on MTurk.
Our system typically reviews your submission within a few minutes and, once approved, you will see it credited to your MTurk account.

5. Contacting Us
Q: How can I contact the requester if I have questions or issues?
A: We handle communication exclusively via the MTurk platform. If you have concerns or run into technical issues, contact us through MTurk’s messaging system.
6. Review and Approval Time
Q: How long until my submission is approved?
A:

We aim to process your submission within a few minutes.
In rare cases (high load or manual checks), it can take longer, but typically it is automated and quick.
